{"summary":"I checked all seven dependents against their predecessors and the original obligations and kept every one unchanged; I wrote no files. I read the full original declaration and specification/project-conformance.md. The fifteen original statements in semantic-assets/stage-0.json and the stage-2 requirement candidates and bindings were a cross-check. Every predecessor's current bytes match its declared digest. I ran no application command, test, verification script or evaluator oracle, and did not read verification/.

How each dependent was checked:

1. design/implementation-design.md (2a5acf0f…), from conformance (148e9bb1…). It cites the conformance document as its authority and defines the minimal module: a named synchronous helloWorld() that, called with no arguments, returns exactly "Hello, world!", with no imports, no default export and no output. It names package.json, src/hello.mjs, design/test-design.md, both test files, test-execution-plan.json and the execution result as separate surfaces, and says the execution result has no file. Excluding output and extra package fields comes from the conformance rule that the only public behaviour is a return value (no stdout, CLI, HTTP, UI or deployment). It is correct, so I kept it.

2. package.json (609158e6…), from the design (2a5acf0f…). It contains exactly "private": true and "type": "module", as the design and the original require. Kept.

3. src/hello.mjs (e62ab9f3…), from the design. It is a named synchronous export returning the exact string, with no imports, default export or output. Kept.

4. design/test-design.md (17fcb06f…), from package.json and src/hello.mjs. Its description of the package fields and the synchronous named export matches the actual bytes. It specifies the component obligation (import helloWorld, strict equality to "Hello, world!") and the UAT obligation (the user-visible greeting contract through the same export, where the user is a JavaScript consumer). Both tests use node:test and node:assert/strict, and neither adds a stdout or CLI surface. Kept.

5. test/component/hello.test.mjs (4eefc997…), from the test design, package.json and src/hello.mjs. It uses node:test and node:assert/strict and has the exact import line. It declares one test named 'component:' that checks helloWorld() by strict equality. It needs no dependency, which fits package.json. Kept.

6. test/uat/hello.uat.test.mjs (42bf7e72…), from the component test, test design, package.json and src/hello.mjs. It has the same import line and assertion style, one test named 'uat:', and adds no output surface. Kept.

7. test-execution-plan.json (c69ed6ca…), from the two tests. Command node with args ["--test", "test/component/hello.test.mjs", "test/uat/hello.uat.test.mjs"]; expectedTestPassCount 2 (one test per file, which is the floor); expectedStdoutMatch "fail 0", which pins no pass count; assertedReturnValue "Hello, world!", the literal both tests assert. Kept.

Because nothing changed, no predecessor digest and no command dependency changed. Construction does not close the original task.","gaps":["The original task is not closed. The independent assessment has not run yet, and acceptance belongs to an owner ruling.","Bindings 10 and 11 (observed execution result and the acceptance rule) remain a separate Executive conjunction. It did not check or rerun C2, so whether the retained execution evidence is current is left to the later owner decision.","Unchanged gap on arguments: nothing specifies or proves what helloWorld() does when called with arguments (req-pressure:07). Other exports and side effects are likewise not proved. I added no contract or test for them.","Unchanged gap on the package.json type field: the planned node --test command does not exercise private or type, since .mjs files load as ES modules regardless of type (req-pressure:19). These fields need their own observation of the actual package.json.","The planned command does not exercise the three documents, the surface set, cross-surface consistency or the ban on copied machinery (req-pressure:18).
